title: Craftsman Database at www.mesda.org
source: Journal of Early Southern Decorative Arts, Vol. 33 (2012)
description: This article introduces the Craftsman Database available at www.mesda.org, a research resource documenting makers of early Southern decorative arts. The database facilitates attribution and identification of artisans across the colonial and federal periods, supporting scholarship on regional styles and the social history of craft production in the American South.
teaser: The Craftsman Database at MESDA (mesda.org) serves as a definitive research instrument for attributing seating, tables, and case pieces to named artisans working across the Early Colonial and Federal periods in the American South. This resource advances the field by linking documentary evidence directly to regional makers, enabling scholars to move beyond stylistic inference toward grounded, archivally supported attribution. Researchers engaged with the social history of Southern craft production and the identification of distinctive regional traditions will find the database an indispensable point of entry.
